relevance_reason: This paper reports the first PAX1 mutation that causes otofaciocervical syndrome in a consanguineous Turkish family, with functional evidence that the mutant protein is hypofunctional.

findings.statement: Pohl et al. (2013) described otofaciocervical syndrome (OFCS) as an autosomal recessive disorder. Its features are facial dysmorphism, external ear anomalies with preauricular pits, hearing impairment, branchial cysts or fistulas, anomalies of the vertebrae and shoulder girdle, and mild intellectual disability.
quotes: Otofaciocervical syndrome (OFCS) is an autosomal recessively inherited disorder characterized by facial dysmorphism, external ear anomalies with preauricular pits and hearing impairment, branchial cysts or fistulas, anomalies of the vertebrae and the shoulder girdle, and mild intellectual disability.

phenotypes.hpo_label: Abnormality of the shoulder girdle musculature

findings.statement: Pohl et al. (2013) studied a large consanguineous Turkish family with OFCS. They performed whole-exome sequencing on a single pooled DNA sample from 4 affected individuals and identified a homozygous c.497G>T mutation in the PAX1 gene. The mutation is predicted to cause a gly166-to-val (G166V) substitution within the highly conserved paired-box domain, and it co-segregated with the disease in the family. Filtering found it to be the only novel homozygous variant.
quotes: In a large consanguineous family with OFCS from Turkey, we performed whole-exome sequencing (WES) of a single pooled DNA sample of four affected individuals.
identified only a single novel homozygous variant, c.497G>T, located in PAX1 that co-segregated with the disease in the family.
The mutation is predicted to substitute the glycine at position 166 to valine (p.G166V) within the highly conserved paired-box domain of the PAX1 protein.

findings.statement: Pohl et al. (2013) used a dual luciferase reporter assay in HEK293T cells to test transactivation of a regulatory sequence in the Nkx3-2 promoter, a direct target of mouse Pax1. Cells expressing the mouse equivalent of the mutation, Pax1(G157V), showed significantly reduced transactivation compared with wildtype Pax1. The authors concluded that this indicated reduced DNA-binding affinity of the mutant protein and that the mutation is hypofunctional.
quotes: We observed a significantly reduced transactivation in HEK293T cells overexpressing Pax1(G157V) in comparison to Pax1(WT) expressing cells, indicating a reduced DNA-binding affinity of the mutant protein.
We performed a dual luciferase reporter assay to examine the transactivation of a regulatory sequence in the Nkx3-2 promoter region, which is a direct target of mouse Pax1 transcriptional regulation.

relevance_reason: This paper reports an EYA1 splice-site point mutation in a patient with otofaciocervical syndrome.

findings.statement: Estefanía et al. (2006) found a single-nucleotide substitution at a splice site of the EYA1 gene in a patient with otofaciocervical syndrome. They concluded that OFC can be caused by point mutations that alter the EYA1 reading frame, not only by major rearrangements. This finding argued against the hypothesis that OFC results from contiguous deletions of EYA1 and adjacent genes.
quotes: we show here that an OFC patient bears a single-nucleotide substitution in a splice site of EYA1
Our results indicate that not only major rearrangements, but also point mutations altering the EYA1 reading frame, can be found in patients with OFC syndrome.

variants.as_reported: single-nucleotide substitution in a splice site of EYA1

findings.statement: Estefanía et al. (2006) described otofaciocervical syndrome as having trophic changes of the face and shoulder girdle in addition to the malformations seen in branchiootorenal syndrome. These malformations are developmental defects of branchial arch structures, the middle and/or inner ear, and the kidney. They noted that it is debated whether OFC and BOR are the same disease.
quotes: OFC is characterized by trophic alterations of the facies and shoulder girdle in addition to the malformations seen in BOR.
shed some light on the controversy over whether OFC and BOR are the same disease

phenotypes.text: trophic alterations of the shoulder girdle

relevance_reason: The paper reports a patient with OFC syndrome who has a de novo large deletion that includes EYA1. This shows that OFC syndrome is allelic with BOR syndrome and is a contiguous gene deletion syndrome.

findings.statement: Rickard et al. (2001) developed a fluorescent quantitative multiplex PCR dosage assay for EYA1 exons 7, 9, and 13. Combined with microsatellite marker analysis, it identified de novo deletions of the EYA1 gene and the surrounding region in 2 patients with complex phenotypes that included features of BOR syndrome. One of these patients, who had OFC syndrome, carried a large deletion of the EYA1 gene region. The authors concluded that this confirmed OFC syndrome is allelic with BOR syndrome.
quotes: This dosage assay, combined with microsatellite marker analysis, has identified de novo deletions of the EYA1 gene and surrounding region in two patients with complex phenotypes involving features of BOR syndrome.
One patient with OFC syndrome carried a large deletion of the EYA1 gene region, confirming that OFC syndrome is allelic with BOR syndrome.

variants.as_reported: large deletion of the EYA1 gene region

findings.statement: Rickard et al. (2001) concluded that OFC syndrome is a contiguous gene deletion syndrome involving EYA1 on 8q13.3. They compared the boundaries of the large deletion in their OFC patient with other reported rearrangements of the region. This narrowed the critical region for Duane syndrome, an eye movement disorder, to the interval between markers D8S553 and D8S1797, a genetic distance of about 1 cM.
quotes: Oto-facio-cervical (OFC) syndrome is a contiguous gene deletion syndrome involving EYA1

Microsatellite analysis has shown that comparison of the boundaries of this large deletion with other reported rearrangements of the region reduces the critical region for Duane syndrome (an eye movement disorder) to between markers D8S553 and D8S1797, a genetic distance of approximately 1 cM.

findings.statement: Rickard et al. (2001) noted that OFC syndrome is clinically similar to branchiootorenal (BOR) syndrome but has clinical features beyond those of BOR syndrome. BOR syndrome is an autosomal dominant disorder involving hearing loss, branchial defects, ear pits, and renal abnormalities.
quotes: Oto-facio-cervical (OFC) syndrome is clinically similar to BOR syndrome, with clinical features in addition to those of BOR syndrome.

relevance_reason: Reports a sporadic patient with otofaciocervical syndrome and argues it is distinct from BOR syndrome.

findings.statement: Dallapiccola and Mingarelli (1995) described a sporadic patient with OFC syndrome. The distinguishing features were a long face with a narrow nose, high-arched palate, prominent and dysmorphic ears, long neck, sloping shoulders and clavicles, winged, low and laterally set scapulae, tetralogy of Fallot, and deafness caused by cochlear malformation. The patient did not have preauricular tags, lacrimal duct stenosis, or renal malformations.
quotes: A sporadic patient with OFC syndrome is described. Distinguishing features were a long face with narrow nose, high arched palate, prominent and dysmorphic ears, long neck, sloping shoulders and clavicles, winged, low, and laterally set scapulae, tetralogy of Fallot, and deafness secondary to cochlear malformation.
The absence of preauricular tags, lacrimal duct stenosis, and renal malformations

findings.statement: Dallapiccola and Mingarelli (1995) noted that some features in the original family, including lateral cervical fistulae, had led to the suggestion that OFC syndrome might be a variant of branchiootorenal (BOR) syndrome. They concluded that their patient supported OFC syndrome being a unique, clinically recognizable entity. Their evidence was that the patient lacked preauricular tags, lacrimal duct stenosis, and renal malformations but had distinct facial and radiographic findings and markedly downward-sloping shoulders.
quotes: Some features present in the original family, including lateral cervical fistulae, have suggested that OFC syndrome could be a variant of BOR syndrome.
the presence of distinct facial and radiographic findings and markedly downward sloping shoulders in the present patient support OFC syndrome being a unique, clinically recognisable entity.
